intro: Monday June 23. The week's most structurally significant session since the June 17 FOMC selloff. Three events today have altered the risk calibration of several long-term theses without changing their fundamental direction: (1) BTC double-bottom ($62,255–$62,313) breached intraday at $61,926 — raises structural questions about whether the post-FOMC accumulation floor holds; (2) SK Hynix triggered circuit breakers twice on KOSPI (-4.6% estimated close ₩2,569,000 from ATH ₩3,000,000 intraday) — Samsung HBM4E competition reports cited; (3) all three macro gates (VIX 17.53, DXY 100.90, SPX futures -1.43%) failed simultaneously. Despite these near-term stresses, the long-term structural drivers remain intact: AI compute demand is in a multi-year supercycle (hyperscaler capex not slowing), HBM shortage extends through 2028 regardless of Samsung competition progress, Starlink compounding toward $20B+ annualized revenue, and Bitcoin's fixed-supply thesis runs on halving cycles not FOMC meetings. The June 24 compound catalyst (NVDA Annual Meeting + Micron Q3 simultaneously) is the conviction reset event for all long-term theses listed below — a Micron beat-and-raise on HBM demand is the single most important structural data point of H1 2026 for every name in this list.

ideas.name: NVIDIA
ideas.idea: The toll road on AI compute — Annual Meeting override active (June 24); 50-DMA ~$206.74 held as structural support through the post-FOMC cycle; June 24 dual catalyst (Annual Meeting + Micron Q3) is the conviction reset; structural accumulation window at $205–$215.
ideas.why: NVDA's fundamental thesis has not changed through the June 23 macro stress: CUDA-locked hyperscaler AI capex remains the most durable structural demand in the semiconductor industry (Google TPU, AWS Trainium, Meta MTIA are inference optimizations, not CUDA replacements). The June 23 session is creating an override-forced entry window at $205–$215 that represents approximately 30x forward FY27 earnings (~$91B revenue consensus) — the cheapest AI-compute-toll-road entry since early 2026. The June 24 compound event (Jensen Huang Annual Meeting 9 AM PT + Micron Q3 HBM confirmation after close) is the framework's final near-term catalyst before the thesis runs to July 29 SK Hynix Q2 / NVDA August earnings. BTC structural breach and SK Hynix circuit breakers create the macro-discount that long-term accumulation frameworks are designed to exploit.
ideas.driver: Hyperscaler + sovereign AI capex compounding through 2028+ (Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, xAI all committed through at least 2027); Vera Rubin rack-scale systems entering production 2026–2027; HBM4E supply chain confirmed sold-out through 2027; CUDA ecosystem moat expanding into robotics and physical AI; 62-analyst consensus PT ~$299 = +43% from ~$209; inference demand following training ramp creates durable second wave.
ideas.risk: Custom ASICs (Google TPU v6, AWS Trainium 3, Meta MTIA 2) erode H100/B200 inference share faster than expected; Micron Q3 miss on HBM revenue signals AI memory demand cycle peaking before Vera Rubin ramp; sustained 30Y above 5.25% structurally compresses AI-capex multiples across the sector.

ideas.name: SK Hynix (000660.KS)
ideas.idea: 12-layer HBM4E confirmed; ADR Nasdaq listing July–August 2026 ($66B total shareholder return); CONVICTION DOWNGRADED TO MEDIUM from HIGH on June 23 due to: (A) circuit-breaker reversal from ₩3,000,000 ATH; (B) Samsung HBM4E competition reports requiring evaluation; (C) estimated -12% close ₩2,569,000.
ideas.why: The circuit-breaker reversal from ₩3,000,000 to ~₩2,569,000 (-12%) in a single session is the pattern of a local top after a parabolic move. The Samsung HBM4E competition reports — while citing no confirmed NVIDIA qualification — represent a credible structural threat that the prior high-conviction framework did not adequately price. SK Hynix's 58% HBM global market share, NVIDIA supply lock through 2030, and HBM4E 12-layer sample leadership remain structural advantages. But the June 23 session introduces a genuine uncertainty: if Samsung achieves NVIDIA HBM4E qualification before SK Hynix completes its own qualification ramp, the market-share premium embedded in the ₩3.0M+ structural valuation is materially compressed. The downgrade to medium reflects the need to monitor this risk before adding. Micron Q3 June 24 is the primary data point: if HBM revenue beats and guidance confirms sold-out through 2027, Samsung competition claims are likely premature.
ideas.driver: HBM4→4E product transition with SK Hynix as performance leader (58% share, 12-layer confirmed, shortage through 2028); NVIDIA supply lock through 2030; ADR Nasdaq listing July–August 2026 creating structural US demand channel ($66B total return including $14B ADR raise + ₩75T+ buyback); mandatory sell-side PT revision cascade from ₩2,690,000 to ₩3.0M+ once Micron Q3 confirms HBM demand; KOSPI 9,000 passive inflow structural bid.
ideas.risk: Samsung executes credible HBM4E capacity ramp with specific NVIDIA qualification announcement before SK Hynix completes qualification (the risk raised by June 23 competition reports); ADR SEC clearance delayed materially beyond June (removes near-term demand catalyst); Micron Q3 HBM miss with Q4 downward guidance directly de-rates SK Hynix on June 25 KST.

ideas.name: Microsoft
ideas.idea: Lowest-risk path to enterprise AI monetization — post-FOMC dip to ~$378 est. is the structural accumulation window; Azure AI workloads compounding regardless of rate path; subscription model insulates against all three macro gates currently failed.
ideas.why: Microsoft's enterprise AI thesis is the most rate-insensitive in the megacap cohort: contracted enterprise Azure bookings at fixed prices for 12–36 months mean Microsoft's near-term revenue is not directly affected by VIX spikes, DXY moves, or SPX futures down -1.43%. The June 23 macro stress that challenges BTC (fixed supply in risk-off) and SK Hynix (equity volatility circuit breakers) does not touch MSFT's contracted enterprise subscription cash flows. Micron Q3 sold-out HBM through 2027 is directly positive for Azure AI workload growth expectations — Azure is one of the primary HBM customers. The Copilot enterprise adoption is compounding across hundreds of millions of seats with pricing power increasing as capabilities improve. At ~$378 post-FOMC, MSFT is the safest vehicle for 3–5 year AI exposure with the lowest framework gate complexity.
ideas.driver: Azure AI workload attach rates compounding; Copilot enterprise adoption across hundreds of millions of seats at increasing pricing tiers; OpenAI relationship providing frontier model differentiation and enterprise AI bundle pricing power; subscription model providing rate-insensitive contracted cash flows; Teams + Dynamics + Power Platform AI integration creating switching-cost reinforced moats.
ideas.risk: AI capex-to-Azure-revenue monetization lag extends beyond H2 2026 (revenue growth deceleration signals); antitrust scrutiny of OpenAI relationship limits bundling opportunities; SPCX Cursor AI (1M+ developers) displaces GitHub Copilot over 2–4 years via AI-native developer tooling category creation.

ideas.name: Alphabet
ideas.idea: Cheapest full-stack AI at the megacap lowest forward multiple — TPU inference cost advantage; June 23 macro-driven discount is the structural accumulation window before the June 24 AI capex confirmation re-rates the cohort.
ideas.why: Alphabet owns Gemini (frontier models), TPUs (cost-competitive inference at scale giving Google Cloud a structural pricing advantage), search (generating the cash to fund everything), and YouTube (second-largest advertising surface). At ~$350–$355 post-FOMC, GOOGL's forward multiple is the lowest in the megacap cohort. The June 23 macro selloff (SPX -1.43% implied) adds to the post-FOMC discount — TPU inference cost leadership is a structural competitive advantage that doesn't deteriorate with VIX moves. Micron Q3 June 24 confirmation that HBM is sold-out through 2027 validates Google Cloud's AI workload infrastructure investments and provides the sector-level conviction reset for all AI monetization names. GOOGL AI Overviews data through Q1 2026 shows session length extending, not falling — the search-moat-extension thesis is validating.
ideas.driver: TPU-driven inference cost advantage creating Google Cloud AI pricing power vs Azure and AWS; Gemini integration across billion-user surfaces (Search, YouTube, Gmail, Maps, Android); Google Cloud AI workload attach rates inflecting upward; potential search-moat expansion rather than AI cannibalization (Q1 2026 session-length data); international advertising revenue benefiting structurally from eventual DXY decline.
ideas.risk: DOJ antitrust remedies fracture the search + advertising bundle (regulatory separation risk unique to GOOGL); AI Overviews prove to be session-length headwind in Q2 2026 data (reversing Q1 thesis); higher-for-longer rates extend multiple compression before AI Overviews thesis compounds.

ideas.name: SpaceX
ideas.idea: Generational franchise with triple-IG validation (Moody's Baa1, Fitch BBB+, S&P BBB) now established as permanent franchise-quality anchors — near-term step-aside maintained (bond distribution, $20B supply overhang, June 22 Day 1 close attempt failed at $165.78); long-term structural thesis unchanged.
ideas.why: SpaceX is the only proven reusable orbital launch system at scale, the only company growing a satellite broadband subscriber base at >40% annually (Starlink 5M+ subscribers), the only entity with confirmed next-generation space logistics economics (Starship), and the only space infrastructure company with Cursor AI ($60B acquisition, 1M+ developer users) adding a recurring software revenue layer not captured in any IG rating agency model. The Moody's Baa1 / Fitch BBB+ / S&P BBB ratings are permanent franchise-quality anchors regardless of near-term price action. June 23 step-aside is the disciplined response to the $20B bond distribution supply overhang and the failed June 22 Day 1 close-above-$185 attempt ($165.78 actual close). The 3–5 year thesis — Starlink $20B+ annualized revenue, Starship 10–50x cost-to-orbit reduction creating a new satellite economy, Cursor AI software layer, Starshield national-security base load — is structurally unaffected by a 2-week bond distribution period.
ideas.driver: Starlink subscriber and ARPU compounding toward $20B+ annualized revenue (5M+ subs, ~$120/month ARPU); Starship cost-to-orbit economics enabling new satellite economy (launch cost reduction 10–50x); Cursor AI software revenue layer (1M+ developers, not in IG rating models); Starshield national-security revenue base providing government contract stability; IG ratings permanently lowering cost of capital; September 2 first earnings = public financial disclosure initiating institutional coverage.
ideas.risk: IPO-cycle overvaluation requires sustained multiple compression before value investors engage (84x revenue at $185 is the most extreme US public equity valuation multiple); September 2 first earnings disappoints vs $2.54T implied market cap expectations; key-person concentration risk (Elon Musk political exposure); December 9 lock-up expiry first major supply event beyond the current bond distribution.

ideas.name: Bitcoin
ideas.idea: CONVICTION DOWNGRADED TO MEDIUM/WATCH from BUY — double-bottom ($62,255–$62,313) breached intraday at $61,926; structural framework shifts from accumulation to 'reduce 50% now, monitor Day 2'; long-term fixed-supply × ETF access × halving thesis intact but near-term support level requires re-establishment.
ideas.why: The June 23 double-bottom breach ($61,926 intraday low) is the first penetration of the structural support that anchored the post-FOMC accumulation thesis. The long-term framework thesis — fixed supply (21M BTC hard cap) × widening institutional access (IBIT AUM compounding) × April 2024 halving supply reduction × DXY structural decline — remains intact on a 2–4 year horizon. But the near-term structural anchor has been compromised, which downgrades the conviction from 'buy the dip' to 'watch for new support establishment.' The two-consecutive-close stop rule (executing on Day 2 June 24 UTC if confirmed) is designed to protect against a structural decline from $62,000 to $55,000–$58,000 (the next major support zone). After the stop executes and a new double-bottom forms in the $60,000–$62,000 zone, the 2–4 year accumulation thesis restarts. The 'watch' designation is the holding pattern between stop execution and re-entry confirmation.
ideas.driver: Fixed supply meeting widening institutional access (ETFs compounding AUM, corporate treasury adoption); DXY structural decline as Hormuz reopening removes oil-inflation driver that anchored dollar strength; IBIT inflows restarting signals institutional accumulation; halving cycle supply reduction (April 2024) creating structural supply deficit; 'digital gold' narrative in Warsh 'no forward guidance' regime creating non-correlated store-of-value demand.
ideas.risk: Day 2 June 24 UTC close below $63,500 triggers full exit; new support in $60,000–$62,000 zone fails to form (structural decline to $55,000–$58,000 next major support); sustained IBIT outflows following double-bottom breach signal institutional de-risking rather than accumulation; Warsh delivers multiple 2026 rate hikes creating sustained DXY above 103.

ideas.name: Amazon
ideas.idea: AWS AI infrastructure + Hormuz logistics tailwind — post-FOMC dip to ~$180 est. is the best megacap cloud entry; Micron Q3 June 24 is the direct AWS AI workload validation event; subscription model insulates against VIX/DXY macro stress.
ideas.why: Amazon runs the world's largest commercial cloud (AWS), is ramping Trainium/Inferentia custom silicon to reduce AI inference costs, and operates the logistics-Prime flywheel that scales into robotic AI fulfillment. Micron Q3 confirmation of sold-out HBM through 2027 directly validates AWS AI workload growth through 2027 — AWS is a primary HBM customer. The Iran ceasefire Hormuz logistics tailwind is Amazon-specific: shipping cost normalization as Hormuz commercial traffic returns reduces Prime delivery margins and fulfillment center costs by an estimated 5–10%. The June 23 macro selloff (SPX -1.43% implied) adds to the post-FOMC discount on AMZN — AWS subscription revenue is contracted and rate-insensitive on a 12–24 month forward basis. At ~$180 post-FOMC, AMZN trades at the lowest valuation relative to AWS revenue growth since the 2022 cloud deceleration.
ideas.driver: AWS AI workload attach rates + Trainium/Inferentia inference cost advantage compounding; Prime and logistics flywheel operational leverage at scale; Hormuz reopening reducing shipping cost inflation 5–10% (Amazon-specific logistics tailwind); AI-native robotics expansion in fulfillment centers; Micron June 24 AWS AI capex validation; Project Kuiper satellite broadband competing with Starlink for enterprise connectivity.
ideas.risk: Cloud spending deceleration if enterprise IT budgets tighten materially in higher-rate environment; competitive pressure from Azure and Google Cloud on enterprise AI workload share; Trainium/Inferentia ramp timelines extending beyond 2027; logistics cost inflation reversing Hormuz-reopening gains if ceasefire fails.
